C3 is the condition to argue about and it must be named ex ante: if inference is competing output capacity sold to the same buyers the builders are already fighting over, the framework does not apply and the correct forecast is Klepper consolidation, not succession.
discriminating_test.value_capture_finding:
HONEST ANSWER: KLEPPER AND THE CAPITAL CYCLE WIN THE GENERAL CASE. THE OPERATOR IS WRONG. The correct resolution is not a compromise but a partition of the state space, plus a third finding that surprises both sides.

FINDING 1 — THE PHRASE 'DIFFERENT PEOPLE' CONFLATES THREE THINGS WITH RADICALLY DIFFERENT BASE RATES, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS THE FRAMEWORK'S ACTUAL CONTENT.
(a) DIFFERENT COST BASIS — the capacity is operated at a basis no builder could have underwritten. HIGH base rate in qualifying cases. This is the real mechanism, and it does not require a new firm: Iridium Satellite LLC is a new entity, but Cogent, NTL becoming Virgin Media, and the recapitalised post-2002 Japanese banks achieve the same thing as the SAME firms with extinguished claims.
(b) DIFFERENT LEGAL ENTITY — medium base rate, and largely an artefact of insolvency law rather than of economics.
(c) DIFFERENT LINEAGE — genuinely new human capital unconnected to the L1/L2 cohort. LOW base rate. Klepper is right. Across the only firm-by-firm datasets that exist — autos, tyres, TV receivers, penicillin — it is 4/4 against, with the 1895-1904 auto cohort's annual exit hazard 76% below the 1910-66 cohort's at age 15 and 90% below at age 25; GM, Ford and Chrysler all descending from Olds, Buick, Cadillac and Ford, which spawned 22 spinoffs and 41 descendants; Walter Chrysler ex-president of Buick; Charles Nash ex-president of GM; and television titled, accurately, "dominance by birthright."
The framework should claim (a) and RETRACT (c). Klepper's own answer to "where do the new people come from" is "the best incumbents' payrolls," and that is fully compatible with (a): a Fairchild or Buick spinoff carries the lineage and carries a new balance sheet.

FINDING 2 — KLEPPER AND THE OPERATOR ARE NOT IN CONTRADICTION; THEY DESCRIBE COMPLEMENTARY REGIONS, AND THE OPERATOR HAS BEEN READING THE RARE REGION AS THE GENERAL RULE. Every Klepper industry, and the Capital Cycle in its entirety, concerns SAME-MARKET OUTPUT CAPACITY. In that structure the only asset is market position; market position cannot change hands cheaply because nobody outside the market wants it; and survivors necessarily win. Klepper goes further and shows the cull is ENDOGENOUS — driven by returns to process R&D scaling with output, not triggered by dominant designs or discrete technological events — so a bubble is not merely insufficient there, it is unnecessary. The modal technologically progressive industry culls 90%+ of its producers with no malinvestment anywhere in the causal chain. The framework's domain is the strict complement: overbuilds whose residue is a general-purpose INPUT to a different downstream industry (C3) and is alienable (C1). There, the buyer is by construction outside the incumbent class, because the incumbents are in the wrong industry to want it. So 'different people' is NOT a signature of the mechanism working. It is a signature of the asset having crossed an industry boundary — and the operator must therefore name that boundary ex ante or the observation is worthless.

FINDING 3 — THE UNCOMFORTABLE ONE, AND THE MOST USEFUL. IN THE BEST-DOCUMENTED QUALIFYING CASES, VALUE DOES NOT ACCRUE TO THE BUYER OF THE ASSET EITHER. Cogent, Level 3 and Zayo bought the fibre and earn utility returns. Netflix and Cloudflare bought metered SERVICES priced off written-down assets and captured the equity value. Iridium is the exception where owner and capturer coincide, and only because the constellation is indivisible and vertically integrated with the service. The general statement is Teece 1986: value accrues to whoever holds the COSPECIALISED COMPLEMENT THAT REMAINS SCARCE AFTER THE INPUT PRICE COLLAPSES. In fibre that was content rights, subscriber relationships and the last mile. In Iridium it was the government and maritime channel plus the $3.5m/month Boeing cost structure. In post-WWI aviation it was the airmail contract — a STATUTORY complement supplying 95% of early carrier revenue at roughly 80% of an $0.80/pound rate, without which the surplus Jennys at $50-100 apiece would have produced barnstormers and nothing else. This prediction differs from both Klepper and the operator, and it has direct prospective bite: after inference prices collapse, value goes to holders of scarce complements — proprietary distribution, regulated data, workflow lock-in, and if C4 is right, firm power and interconnection — not to whoever buys distressed accelerators and not to a new cohort of model labs.

FINDING 4 — THE FIRE-SALE PROBLEM MUST BE CONCEDED AND THEN ANSWERED, NOT WAVED AWAY. Ramey and Shapiro measured displaced aerospace capital selling to INDUSTRY INSIDERS at a 29-40% premium over outsiders, up to roughly 100% for newer machine tools, with Shleifer and Vishny explaining why. In the only direct measurement available, outsider acquisition is the LOW-VALUE allocation. The framework and the fire-sale literature therefore predict the identical observable with opposite welfare signs, and the framework cannot keep treating outsider acquisition as self-evidently the mechanism working. The answer is that the identity of the buyer is NOT the confirming evidence — POST-TRANSFER PHYSICAL UTILISATION is. Iridium passes: constellation switched off in 2000, profitable by 2005, 19% EBITDA growth in 2010, $135m free cash flow. Ebone passes: dark network relit, EUR 15m to $2.3bn. Aerospace 1988-95 fails, and it fails on C2 (output demand died), which is why the gate excludes it correctly. Separately, Eisfeldt-Rampini should be conceded as directionally hostile but not decisive: it measures VOLUME of reallocation, dominated by going-concern transactions within the incumbent class, while the framework requires ownership-class turnover, which nobody has measured separately. Claim the reconciliation, flag it as untested rather than established, and run the decomposition.

BOTTOM LINE FOR THE OPERATOR. Delete 'usually DIFFERENT PEOPLE.' Replace with: "Value accrues to the holder of the scarce cospecialised complement after the input price resets — usually neither the builder nor the buyer of the written-down capacity, and only a new cohort when the capacity has crossed an industry boundary, which is rare." On this corpus that is roughly three cases in thirty.
discriminating_test.what_the_framework_cannot_do:
1. IT CANNOT PICK THE THIRD ORDER. Farmer-Lafond forecasts the unit cost of an ALREADY-NAMED artefact with calibrated error bars — a real and rare achievement, and it works precisely because cost curves are smooth difference-stationary random walks with drift, i.e. the ABSENCE of the discontinuous layer-jump the cascade requires. It forecasts nothing about which artefact, about application emergence, about adoption, or about value capture. (Note the framework's own citation is wrong: F&L 2016 fit a time-based Moore model to 53 technologies; the Wright-versus-Moore horse race is Nagy, Farmer, Bui and Trancik 2013 on 62 technologies, finishing roughly tied.) Product space is worse: Li and Neffke, searching tens of thousands of specifications on US city-industry data, find relatedness predicts where industries ARE far better than where they GROW — among the most negative-residual city-industries, the growth-spurt rate is 3.36% against a 2.68% base rate. The framework may claim EXCLUSION power. It may not claim SELECTION power. Anyone using it to pick winners is misusing it.

2. IT CANNOT CLAIM THE BUBBLE IS NECESSARY. Four hyperscale third orders in this corpus were built with no L2 bust: Alibaba and Tencent cloud (organic cash-flow build 1998-2009, no fire sale, no distressed carrier assets, in sharp contrast to the AWS story the operator tells); India Stack (continuous liberalisation 1991-2016, roughly $100bn cumulative telecom capex with no bust cycle, Aadhaar 2009, UPI April 2016); M-PESA (a GBP 1m DFID grant, greenfield on Safaricom's existing SMS platform, 24% of Kenyan GDP flowing through it by 2012); Brazil Pix (central-bank decree, 16 November 2020, fastest adoption in the world at roughly 60% of adults in two years). Add Unit 8200 (steady-state demobilisation, no distress event of any kind) and BASF/Bayer/Hoechst (aspirin 1899 and Haber-Bosch 1909 with zero change of hands). The framework is a theory of ONE route, and not the most common one.

3. IT CANNOT EVEN CLAIM THE BUBBLE IS CHARACTERISTIC. Goldfarb, Kirsch and Miller find TOO LITTLE entry in the dot-com era, not overbuild: five-year survival approached 50%, at or above other emerging industries in their formative years, and survival was unrelated to receipt or amount of private equity. Goldfarb and Kirsch show bubbles are a financing-environment phenomenon most important technologies never exhibit. Combined with the Cogent, Internap and Southwest corrections from round 1, the 'productive bubble' leg is now the weakest part of the structure and must be demoted from mechanism to occasional accompaniment.

4. IT CANNOT DATE ANYTHING, AND THE 'DECADES' CLAIM IS FALSE. Golder and Tellis: median lag from pioneer entry to the eventual long-run share leader is about 13 years within a product category. Gort-Klepper Stage I duration fell from 23.1 years for pre-1930 products to 4.9 years for post-1940 — so any framework asserting a constant multi-decade lag is falsified by that time series alone. Observed lags in this corpus run from 2 years (Iridium: bankruptcy August 1999, asset sale and relaunch March 2001) to 30-40 years (electrification), with Nokia-to-Supercell at 3 years and arguably negative. That dispersion means the lag carries no information and must not be used as a screen. The framework must be restated as a mechanism claim with NO periodicity content — it fails all four of Rosenberg and Frischtak's requirements as currently stated.

5. IT DOES NOT SURVIVE CONTACT WITH ITS OWN CANONICAL EXAMPLES. Example (a) breaks at three of four joints, and the blow comes from the framework's own authorities: David and Wright treat the assembly line as a converging trajectory, not a derivative, and note that automated materials handling did not require electrification. The WWII tail must be cut outright — Field measures manufacturing TFP falling at -5.1% per year 1941-45, and the capacity was federally financed and mostly not retained by the firms that operated it. What survives is narrower and cleaner: L1 practical electric power 1880s-1900s, L2 a twenty-year no-payoff group-drive retrofit 1899-1919 plus a utility holding-company frenzy roughly 1922-1932, L3 the 1919-29 reorganisation on unit drive and single-storey layout delivering industrial TFP near 5-6%/yr against roughly 1% before. Example (b) must be SPLIT: the video/CDN chain survives and is quantifiable; the cloud/SaaS chain is falsified by the ASP-to-SaaS natural experiment. AWS and Azure come off the list. Cloudflare (2009) is the only well-chosen name on it. Two statistics must be struck: the '2.7% dark fibre' figure (a misquoted single-city datapoint) and any telecom-skills claim (no public tracing of WorldCom, Global Crossing or 360networks engineers exists, and carrier employment never recovered).

6. IT HAS NO SLOT FOR A MANDATORY NON-BUBBLE INTERMEDIATE LAYER. Streaming was impossible without DOCSIS 3.0 and FiOS at roughly $23bn from incumbent cash flow, H.264, Flash's December 2007 H.264 build, Silverlight, Roku and the Xbox. None of that is malinvestment residue. A theory that cannot represent a necessary, capital-intensive, non-bubble layer between L2 and L3 is not a theory of how value arrives; it is a theory about one contributing input.

7. IT CANNOT TELL REALLOCATION FROM CONGESTION WITHOUT C3, AND IT CANNOT TELL ITSELF FROM A FIRE SALE WITHOUT A RETROSPECTIVE TEST. Chapter 11 manufactures zombies whenever the written-down asset is competing output capacity in the same product market — US airlines are the standing domestic mirror of Caballero-Hoshi-Kashyap. And the only instrument that separates the mechanism from ordinary fire-sale value destruction is post-transfer utilisation, which requires data that by construction does not exist until years after the transfer. On the mechanism question the framework is retrospective by necessity.

8. IT CANNOT ACCOMMODATE INSTITUTIONAL THIRD ORDERS WITHOUT CHANGING ITS ONTOLOGY. Aglietta inverts example (a)'s sequence: the Fordist transformation of the labour process long preceded any rise in working-class consumption, and Fordism-as-regime was an institutional settlement won by 1930s-40s labour struggle and collective bargaining, not a technological consequence. Gramsci named it contemporaneously in 1929-30, so the 'decades of lag before anyone sees it' claim fails on the operator's own flagship case. Either example (a) is retired or the framework must admit political settlement as a first-class third-order generator — in which case Piore and Sabel's contingent industrial divide, not a determinate cascade, is the right ontology. The Kelly Act and NTT unbundling make the same point from the other direction: in two of the framework's better cases, the enabling act is a statute.

9. THE 'NOBODY FORECASTS THE THIRD ORDER' DEFENCE IS DEAD. Gilder, HP's 1998 Utility Computing Division, Sun Grid at $1/CPU-hour in March 2006, and Hastings naming Netflix in 1997 were all ex ante and right in kind. The forecasters and the incumbents who acted on them were destroyed anyway. That is net GOOD for the mechanism — it independently confirms that foresight is not the scarce input — and fatal to any claim that this framework confers unique foresight.

10. WHAT IT CAN ACTUALLY DO, STATED AT THE CEILING OF THE EVIDENCE: given a named metered input, a documented build-justifying price, and a named candidate downstream business, it can (i) EXCLUDE infeasible adjacencies with meaningful precision, (ii) bound the cost trajectory of an already-named artefact with calibrated error bars, (iii) predict WHICH parts of an overbuild transfer and appreciate and which are scrapped (the substrate/overlay split), and (iv) score whether a price reset will persist beyond one asset replacement cycle. It cannot name the winner, it cannot date the win, it cannot tell you a bubble is coming or is required, and on this corpus the full phenomenon it describes occurs roughly once in ten candidate episodes.

## 4. REGISTRATION AI-3 — TOKENS, AND THE WRIGHT'S LAW INSTRUMENT

**Metered input P.** Two series, registered separately because **they move in opposite directions and conflating them is the single most common error in this domain**:

- **P_cap** = cheapest blended (3:1 in:out) $/M tokens for any model at or above a **fixed, ex-ante capability threshold**. Threshold definitions locked now: *"GPT-4-class" := ≥ the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score attained by GPT-4o as of 1 Jan 2025.* *"Frontier-2026-class" := ≥ the AA index score of the highest-scoring model on 1 Aug 2026 (the Claude Opus 5 / GPT-5.6-Sol tier)* `[V, artificialanalysis.ai/models]`.
- **P_task** = $ per *completed task* at frontier capability, for three named tasks (below). This series falls far more slowly than P_cap, because reasoning budgets are rising as fast as per-token prices fall.

**Fitted rate for P_cap (the Farmer–Lafond / Nagy-Farmer-Bui-Trancik instrument, used within its licence).** Anchors: Mar-2023 GPT-4 blended $37.5/M → Nov-2023 GPT-4-Turbo $15/M → May-2024 GPT-4o $7.5/M → Jul-2024 GPT-4o-mini $0.26/M → 2025 $0.10–0.15/M → **Aug-2026 ≈ $0.05/M `[E — pin from AA archive]`**.

**F3(i) Post-transfer utilisation (Bernstein–Colonnelli–Iverson design).** For each transfer scored above, physical utilisation must **rise** after transfer.
- Registered: rises for AI shells/substations (2027–31); rises for B2 lab-to-GMP conversions; rises for B3 office-to-residential; **falls or stays flat for distressed accelerators**; **falls for LEO satellites**.
